title: Progressive traffic taper + session escrow for active-active gateway streaming resilience
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: This ticket implements a progressive traffic tapering mechanism combined with a session escrow layer at the edge gateway to enable active-active multi-region failover for streaming sessions. The goal is to shift traffic between regions with minimal client-visible disruption, preserve in-flight KV cache/state where possible, and provide deterministic fallbacks when capacity or latency SLOs are threatened.

Background: We observed two classes of failures during the last outage: (1) abrupt region drains caused streaming sessions to terminate unexpectedly and clients to retry, leading to double-billing and state loss; (2) overloaded replicas tripped coarse-grained circuit breakers that ejected healthy sessions. Current failover logic is binary (drain now or not) and does not coordinate with session state or streaming handover.

Proposal: 1) Progressive traffic taper: instead of immediate 100% cutover, the gateway will shift traffic using a parameterized taper curve (default: 80-60-40-20-0 over configurable windows). Each step is telemetry gated by SLO headroom, tail-latency, and KV cache pressure metrics. 2) Session escrow: when a session is nominated for handoff, the edge creates an ephemeral escrow record containing minimal rehydration artifacts (session id, last-offset, lightweight summary, pointer to persisted KV snapshot). Escrow is replicated to a cross-region durable store for short TTLs (60s by default). 3) Stream handshake: clients are offered a 2-phase resume token and a graceful short-buffer period where the old region continues to accept and forward tokens while the new region warms caches. 4) Soft circuit breakers: circuit decisions move from replica-level hard ejects to a graded throttling model (token-shed -> priority-degrade -> eviction) driven by SLO budgets and per-session criticality.

Why this is different: The design prioritizes session integrity and streamed-token continuity over aggressive capacity-preserving ejections. It treats failover as a multi-step choreography rather than an instantaneous state flip, reducing duplicate work and improving p99 tail latency during transitions.
acceptance_criteria: Can shift 1000 concurrent streaming sessions from region A to region B with <=1% session-abandon and <200ms median additional resume latency
Escrow store writes and reads succeed under normal traffic and are garbage-collected after TTL; no escrow leakage after 5 minutes
Tapering steps are telemetry gated: transitions abort within 5s if tail-latency > configured threshold
Soft circuit-breaker phases (throttle -> degrade -> evict) occur deterministically based on configured thresholds and generate incident telemetry
Automated e2e test reproducing a regional capacity overload validates session resume semantics and no double-billing
implementation_notes: Edge gateway: add taper controller with weighted-shift API and per-route session tagging
Session escrow service: small footprint service (k8s deployment) with cross-region replication using existing durable tier (S3-backed index + 1s-2s replication window)
KV snapshot: integrate with existing prefix/KV cache persistence hooks to write minimal rehydration blobs
Client contract: add resume-token header and backoff handshake; SDKs must be backward compatible (server will support both modes)
Circuit-breaker refactor: replace hard-eject path with phased actions and add hysteresis to prevent flapping
rollout_plan: 1) Canary: enable taper controller (read-only) in us-west-2 on 5% of traffic for 24h; collect metrics
2) Small-scale: enable progressive taper + escrow for non-production orgs and internal loadtest harness; run synthetic 2k concurrent streams
3) Regional: enable for low-traffic customer region and exercise telemetry gates
4) Gradual: ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on SLO regressions
5) Post-rollout: run 72h soak and add to chaos playbook for periodic exercises
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Escrow store becomes hot during mass failover -> Mitigation: shard escrow keys by session hash and enforce write QPS throttles
Risk: Clients without updated SDKs might not support resume token -> Mitigation: maintain compatibility path where old clients get force-evicted with clear retry guidance and metrics tagged
Risk: Incorrect taper curve config causes oscillation -> Mitigation: add damping/hysteresis and require two-step opt-in for curve changes in prod
Risk: Cross-region replication lag causes stale rehydration -> Mitigation: minimum warmup window and verify KV snapshot freshness before final cutover
qa_notes: Create synthetic harness to open 10k streaming connections and trigger staged drain; verify resume success rate and session continuity
Unit test escrow TTL GC and replication fences; add property tests for resume-token idempotency
Load test soft circuit-breaker path for 30m at 2x normal traffic to observe graded degradation behavior
